h1: The 6 Best TP-Link Network Switches of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six TP-Link switches from a 5-port Gigabit to a 48-port managed PoE+ model, compared on speed, PoE budget, ports and warranty.
summary: The TL-SG105 is the default for a home desk, the TL-SG1005P adds PoE+ for cameras and access points, and the 2.5G TL-SG105S-M2 and TL-SG108S-M2 suit faster internet plans. The TL-SG3452P is the managed option for larger installs.
intro: The classic switch mistake is buying ports you will never fill while ignoring the speed of the ports you will use. A cheap Gigabit switch quietly caps a 2.5G internet plan or a 2.5G NAS.

We ranked six TP-Link switches from the spec sheets, weighing port speed, PoE budget, port count, management features and warranty length. We reviewed what each listing states rather than benchmarking throughput.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG105 5-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: The plug-and-play five-port switch that fits most desks.
products.description:
The TL-SG105 has 5 Gigabit ports with QoS and IGMP snooping, a metal desktop or wall-mount case and a 3-year warranty. It costs under $25.

It lands here since it covers the most common need at the lowest price. The 2.5G models below it are faster but cost more, and only help if the rest of your gear is also 2.5G.

Buy it for a home desk or a small TV cabinet. The caveat is that every port is capped at Gigabit.
products.idealFor: Desks and small setups with Gigabit gear.
products.skipIf: You have a 2.5G plan or devices.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG1005P 5-Port Gigabit PoE Switch
products.verdict: Powers four PoE+ devices from one box with 65W total.
products.description:
The TL-SG1005P has 4 PoE+ ports sharing 65W total plus one uplink, with QoS and IGMP snooping and a 3-year warranty. It falls in the $25 to $50 bracket.

Where it sits comes down to the fact that it adds PoE to the SG105 formula. The 65W total budget is the limit: four power-hungry devices can exceed it.

Best for a few cameras or an access point. Check each device's wattage against 65W.
products.idealFor: Small camera or access point setups.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG105S-M2 5-Port 2.5G Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Five 2.5G ports that run over existing Cat5e cabling.
products.description:
The TL-SG105S-M2 has 5 ports at 2.5G with 25Gbps switching capacity in a compact metal case. It works over existing Cat5e and sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

The ordering here reflects that 2.5G only pays off with matching gear. Against the SG105 it costs more but removes the Gigabit ceiling.

Buy it if your router, NAS or PC already has 2.5G. Skip it if everything else is Gigabit.
products.idealFor: Anyone with a 2.5G router or NAS.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG108S-M2 8-Port 2.5G Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Eight fanless 2.5G ports for a growing multi-device setup.
products.description:
The TL-SG108S-M2 has 8 ports at 2.5G with 40Gbps capacity and a fanless, unmanaged design. It works over existing Cat5e and sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Its position follows from the fact that it is the same idea as the 5-port 2.5G model with more ports and a higher bracket.

Best for a home lab with several 2.5G devices. Do not buy it for only two or three devices.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG116 16-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Sixteen Gigabit ports for a crowded closet.
products.description:
The TL-SG116 has 16 Gigabit ports with QoS and IGMP snooping, a 0 to 40 degree operating range and a 3-year warranty. Price lands from $50 to $100.

Fifth place reflects that because it offers volume rather than speed. The 2.5G switches above are faster per port.

Best for a wired home with many devices. The 0 to 40 degree range matters in a warm closet.

products.name: TP-Link TL-SG3452P 48-Port L2+ Managed PoE Switch
products.verdict: A 48-port managed PoE+ switch for large installs.
products.description:
The TL-SG3452P has 48 PoE+ ports sharing 384W, L2+ management, 4 SFP slots, static routing and a 5-year warranty. It falls in the $500+ bracket.

It ranks last for a general audience because it is far more switch than a home needs. For a business or large lab, it leads the list on features.

Buy it for offices and campuses. A home user would pay for ports and management they never use.
products.idealFor: Offices and large installs needing management.

whatMatters.detail: Port speed is the maximum data rate per port, either 1Gbps or 2.5Gbps here. A Gigabit switch caps a faster router or NAS. Check the listing for the per-port speed, not only the total capacity.
PoE sends power over the Ethernet cable. The total budget is shared across ports, so 65W covers a few devices but not many. Add up each device's wattage before buying.
Unmanaged switches work on plug-in. Managed switches add routing and VLAN control. Most homes do not need management.
Buy a few more ports than you need today. Extra ports cost little, but replacing a full switch costs more.
Warranties here run from 3 to 5 years. A metal case and fanless design help with heat and noise. Check both on the listing.

faq.q: Will a 2.5G switch work with Gigabit devices?
faq.a: Our listings do not cover this in detail, but 2.5G switches generally negotiate lower speeds. Check the listing to confirm backward compatibility.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with switches?
faq.a: Overbuying ports or ignoring speed. Match port speed to your fastest device.

faq.q: Is the TL-SG1005P worth it over the TL-SG105?
faq.a: Yes if you have PoE devices, thanks to four PoE+ ports at 65W total. If not, the SG105 is cheaper.

faq.q: Do I need new cables for 2.5G?
faq.a: The 2.5G models here are listed as working over existing Cat5e cabling.

faq.q: How do I keep a switch cool?
faq.a: Give it airflow. The TL-SG116 lists a 0 to 40 degree C operating range.

faq.q: Can the SG3452P be used at home?
faq.a: It can, but it is built for large installs with 48 PoE+ ports and management.

finalTake: For most people the TL-SG105 is the right switch. Add PoE with the TL-SG1005P, or move to 2.5G with the TL-SG105S-M2 if your gear supports it. The TL-SG3452P is for managed, large-scale installs only.
